subject: Materials Science
title: Digital Image Correlation
description: Learn Digital Image Correlation in one minute.

hook.text: Paint a random speckle pattern on a part, load it, and cameras track every dot — mapping strain across the surface.

buildup.text: DIC compares images before and during loading — software calculates displacement and strain at every point.

discovery.text: It provides full-field strain maps — no strain gauge needed, and you see the whole picture at once.

twist.text: DIC is non-contact and works at any scale — from microchips under a microscope to bridges under traffic.

climax.text: Aerospace engineers validate finite element models by comparing DIC strain maps to simulation predictions.

punchline.text: A speckle pattern and two cameras turn any surface into a sensor.

quiz.question: What does digital image correlation measure?
options: The chemical composition of a surface
Full-field surface displacement and strain by tracking patterns
The internal temperature of the material
